title: Tech Note: 4D Advanced Debugging Techniques – Part 2
author: Josh Fletcher, Technical Support Engineer, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: Custom debug logging (function/procedure/method-level logging with stack-level indentation)

historical_commentary.text: This note presents a custom text-file logging technique and an accompanying open-source '4D Logger 2004-1' component as an alternative debugging strategy for cases where 4D's native debugger/Runtime Explorer/error messages aren't available or sufficient — notably for compiled databases, timing/synchronization bugs, and pattern-recognition-style investigation across process IDs. The core insight, that structured logging with stack-level indentation and process IDs reveals patterns invisible to a live debugger (especially for concurrency bugs), is a durable, still-relevant debugging technique used across all of software development today, even though the specific 4D component and compiled-vs-interpreted framing are dated to 4D's pre-ORDA, pre-Project-Mode era.
related_updates: 4D has since added more modern debugging and logging facilities (e.g., improved Runtime Explorer, structured logging commands) beyond what was available in 4D 2004
The general practice of structured, stack-level, process-tagged logging for diagnosing timing/concurrency bugs remains standard practice in modern software development generally
